CAUSE: The Claude CLI is already dead, but its SDK client is still attached to the session. During a cross-runtime switch, `_change_runtime_chat_locked()` calls `_disconnect_backend()`. That calls `ClaudeBackend.disconnect()`, which re-raises any exception from `client.disconnect()`. The switch catches it and returns `text_tail_source_release_failed` before changing the model. Retrying repeats the same cleanup failure.

Evidence: `app/session.py` in `_change_runtime_chat_locked()` maps disconnect exceptions to this error; `_disconnect_backend()` leaves `self._backend` attached if `backend.disconnect()` raises. In `app/backend_claude.py`, `ClaudeBackend.disconnect()` clears `_client` in `finally` but re-raises the SDK error, so the session retains the stale backend. The dead process explains the cleanup failure; the code’s unconditional propagation makes that failure block the switch.

Fix recommended: make disconnect tolerate an already-exited CLI process, while still cleaning up client and MCP config. Also ensure `_disconnect_backend()` clears the session’s backend reference in a `finally` block when the backend has relinquished its client. This should let the switch proceed while retaining the text-tail history transfer.
